question: to the Commission Lukas Mandl (PPE) Subject:

As humanitarian crises intensify, hunger is on the rise, with serious consequences for children and adults alike, as well as for global developments migration to radicalisation. Contributions from key development cooperation partners to the UN World Food Programme have decreased in recent times. The United Nations’ contribution fell from around UD 4.44 billion in 2024 to around USD 2.06 billion in 2025. Contributions also decreased in Europe. Those of the EU decreased from around EUR 550.3 million in 2024 to around EUR 520.1 million in 2025. Member States’ contributions decreased from around EUR 1.65 billion to around EUR 1.09 billion. 1.
Since the reply to the 2025 question1, what concrete steps has the Commission taken to deepen cooperation with the United States on food security, addressing root causes of migration and support?
Does the European Union already have a coordinated strategy with the United States to combat hunger?

In light of the decline in contributions from key development cooperation partners, what steps are being taken to ensure that the World Food Programme remains operational in humanitarian crises and to strengthen Europe’s role in ensuring global food security?
https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-10-2025-001091_EN.html.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.8.2026) The European Commission shares the concern over the worsening global food security situation and the impact of declining funding on the most vulnerable populations. Cooperation with the US on food security has traditionally been smooth and conducted through relevant multilateral fora, including the G7, G20, the Global Network Against Food Crises or the Food Assistance Convention, which provide channels for exchanging on priorities and coordinated action. The Commission continues to welcome cooperation with the US on humanitarian action. The EU’s response is guided by humanitarian needs and adapted to each crisis context. Depending on needs, local capacities, market conditions and operational constraints, assistance may include food or cash support, nutrition interventions, and measures to protect livelihoods and strengthen resilience. Between 2022 and 2025, the Commission provided more than EUR 3.1 billion for humanitarian food and nutrition assistance. In recent years, the World Food Programme (WFP) has consistently been the largest recipient of Commission humanitarian funding, reflecting its central role in delivering life-saving assistance. Through its regular Strategic Dialogue with WFP, the Commission discusses shared priorities, operational challenges and ways to strengthen cooperation. This close engagement helps safeguard life-saving operations and promote timely, flexible and predictable funding, while supporting preparedness, anticipatory action and, where appropriate, resilience building.
